meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: case forms
the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: очень приятно = pleased to meet you

examples.text: Очень приятно. А в чём дело?
examples.trans: Pleased to meet you. So what's the matter?

познакомиться.gloss: to get acquainted, to meet (for the first time)

meanings.en: to meet for the first time, to get acquainted
meanings.note: + с + instrumental

examples.trans: I dreamed of meeting your friends.

examples.text: А как вы с ней познакомились?
examples.trans: And how did you meet her?

meanings.note: Prefix 'вз-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'аимно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Это слово «взаимно» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'likewise' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: + genitive
literally 'until the meeting'
= Enjoy your meal!
= Enjoy your meal!

examples.trans: Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
e.g. a school evening

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: in questions
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: a person of no consequence

examples.text: Всё, у меня денег совсем в ноль.
examples.trans: That's it, my money is completely down to zero.

examples.text: Самсон, ты ведь тоже уже в ноль.
examples.trans: Samson, you are also already at zero after all.

examples.text: Наша команда ведёт в счёте два ноль!
examples.trans: Our team is leading in the score two-nil!

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: with masculine and neuter nouns (две with feminine); the noun goes into the genitive singular: два месяца

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: the noun after it goes into the genitive singular

examples.trans: We give him three days. That's it.

meanings.note: + genitive singular: четыре года

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: followed by the genitive plural: пять тысяч

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

meanings.note: Core Russian num meaning 'six' in everyday speech.
+ genitive plural: семь тысяч; сорок семь = forty-seven

examples.text: Там депозит на семь тысяч рублей!
examples.trans: There's a deposit for seven thousand roubles!

examples.text: Семь тысяч, давай сходим! Ты же любишь морепродукты.
examples.trans: Seven thousand, let's go! After all, you love seafood.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'семь').
